memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "The priest is to examine the affected area and isolate the article for seven days. On the seventh day he is to examine it, and if the mould has spread in the fabric, the woven or knitted material, or the leather, whatever its use, it is a persistent defiling mould; the article is unclean." - Lev 13:50-51 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The same rhythm we have seen all through this chapter: examine, isolate, wait, look again. God applies to a coat the same patient care He applied to a person.

There is a discipline here that our age has almost lost. We want instant verdicts. We form opinions in seconds and publish them before we have looked twice. Something appears online and we have concluded, condemned and moved on within a minute.

But God's way is slow. Look, wait, look again.

That patience is worth building into our lives deliberately. Before responding to that message, wait until morning. Before concluding what someone meant, ask them. Before making the decision, give it a week. Proverbs says: the one who gives an answer before he listens — this is foolishness and disgrace (Prov 18:13).

Notice too the phrase whatever its use. It did not matter how valuable or useful the article was. Usefulness never exempted anything from examination.

We sometimes protect things in our lives because they are productive — a working relationship, a lucrative arrangement, a ministry that is bearing fruit. But usefulness is not the same as cleanness. God examines everything, including the things that are working well.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Where do you tend to rush to judgement?
2. Is there something in your life you have protected from examination because it is useful?
3. What would building a "wait and look again" habit change for you?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, slow me down. Give me patience before I conclude, and let nothing in my life be exempt from Your examination — not even the things that seem to be working. Amen.
